# UML Class Diagram

Insert/draw UML here. Include defensible relationships and multiplicities.

- **Patient 1 — 0.. Appointment:\*** A patient starts with no appointments and can accumulate many over time via walk-ins, follow-ups, cancellations kept in history, but every appointment must belong to exactly one patient.
- **Practitioner 1 — 0.. Appointment:\*** Same logic from the other side, a practitioner may have no appointments yet or many, but each appointment is tied to exactly one practitioner as per the no double booking requirement outlined in the brief.
- **Receptionist 1 — 0.. Appointment (manages):\*** One receptionist can manage many appointments over a shift/day. I have selected the "1" multiplicity on the receptionist side because we're not modelling multiple receptionists jointly managing a single appointment. (Although an assumption can be made here, that if there is more than one receptionist at this clinic that all receptionists would have the ability to manage a single appointment).

# Design Rationale

Explain class selection, responsibility allocation and key relationships.

**Classes**: The four classes Patient, Practitioner, Receptionist and Appointment were selected as they are specifically stated in the brief and are directly evidenced by the functional requirements. Each of these Classes have their own ID, Attributes and Behaviours.

**Responsibility allocation**: Reflects the requirements and actions that each class can perform. Each class owns and reports its own state, but changes are triggered by their respective collaborators. Receptionists and Practitioners instruct these changes; Appointment applies these changes and updates the displays.

**Key Relationships**: Patient 1–0..\* Appointment and Practitioner 1–0..\* Appointment, every appointment belongs to exactly one of each, supporting the no double booking rule, and Receptionist 1–0..\* Appointment "manages" as an operational link. As stated previously, this is working on the assumption of only one Receptionist.
